title: Notice of Violation and Enforcement Action – HOA Covenant Breach
text:
HOMEOWNERS ASSOCIATION OF WILLOW CREEK ESTATES

NOTICE OF VIOLATION AND ENFORCEMENT ACTION

Cause No. 2024-CV-07893

To: Mr. Jonathan P. Hargrove and Ms. Linda Hargrove
123 Meadowlark Lane
Austin, Texas 78701

From: Willow Creek Estates Homeowners Association, Inc.
Date: March 15, 2025

RE: Violation of Section 3.2(a) of the Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, and Restrictions

Dear Mr. Hargrove and Ms. Hargrove:

This letter constitutes formal notice that you are in violation of the governing documents of the Willow Creek Estates Homeowners Association (the “Association”). Specifically, Section 3.2(a) of the Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, and Restrictions (the “CC&Rs”) provides:

“§ 3.2(a) No owner shall maintain any structure, fence, wall, or other improvement upon any lot without prior written approval of the Architectural Review Committee. Any improvement constructed without such approval shall be subject to removal at the owner’s expense.”

The unauthorized fence erected along the rear property line of Lot 42, as recorded in the Bexar County Deed Records, Volume 1234, Page 567, constitutes a breach of this provision. The fence, constructed of untreated lumber, was first observed by Association inspector David M. Reyes on February 10, 2025. You were previously warned in a letter dated February 20, 2025, but have failed to cure the violation.

Pursuant to Texas Property Code § 202.001, et seq., the Association may levy fines, impose liens, and seek injunctive relief. A hearing before the Association’s Board of Directors is scheduled for April 10, 2025, at 7:00 p.m. at the Willow Creek Community Center, 4500 Creek Bend Drive, Austin, Texas. You have the right to attend and present evidence.

The Association has retained counsel, Mr. Robert T. Channing of Channing & Associates, PLLC, 100 Congress Avenue, Suite 200, Austin, Texas 78701, telephone (512) 555-0199, email r.channing@channinglawfirm.com. Please direct all correspondence to Mr. Channing.

If you fail to comply within thirty (30) days, the Association will file a lawsuit in the 261st Judicial District Court of Travis County, Texas, styled Willow Creek Estates Homeowners Association, Inc. v. Jonathan Hargrove and Linda Hargrove, Docket No. D-1-GN-25-001234. The Association may seek an order for removal of the fence, damages, and attorney’s fees. A similar case, Highland Hills HOA v. Martinez, 456 S.W.3d 789 (Tex. App.—Austin 2015), affirmed the authority of HOAs to enforce aesthetic covenants. See also In re Willow Creek HOA Assessment Dispute, 789 S.W.3d 123 (Tex. App.—Austin 2022).

Your Social Security numbers on file with the Association are: Linda: 456-78-9012; Jonathan: 456 78 9013. Your date of birth as provided in your membership application: Jonathan: March 7, 1975; Linda: August 22, 1977.

If you have any questions, please contact the Association’s property manager, Ms. Karen S. O’Donnell, at (512) 555-0142 or k.odonnell@willowcreekhoa.org.

Sincerely,

Willow Creek Estates Homeowners Association, Inc.
By: Margaret L. Sullivan, President

Enclosures: Copy of CC&Rs, Violation Report, Photo Evidence

Secretary’s Note: This notice is sent pursuant to the authority granted in the Bylaws. The minor A.B., residing at 124 Meadowlark Lane, is not a party to this enforcement action.

title: Notice of Intent to Lien and Foreclose – Delinquent Assessments
text:
SUNFLOWER RIDGE HOMEOWNERS ASSOCIATION, INC.

NOTICE OF INTENT TO LIEN AND FORECLOSE

Cause No. 2025-CV-00142

To: Mr. William T. Ferguson III and Ms. Patricia A. Ferguson
890 Oak Hollow Drive
Houston, Texas 77002

From: Sunflower Ridge Homeowners Association, Inc.
Date: April 2, 2025

RE: Delinquent Assessments – Lot 15, Block B, Sunflower Ridge Subdivision

Dear Mr. Ferguson and Ms. Ferguson:

This is to inform you that as of the date of this letter, your account with the Sunflower Ridge Homeowners Association (the “Association”) is delinquent in the amount of $4,567.89, representing unpaid regular assessments, special assessments, late fees, and interest for the period from January 1, 2024, through March 31, 2025.

Pursuant to Texas Property Code § 209.009, a homeowners association may foreclose its lien on a property owner’s lot for failure to pay assessments. The statute states in part:

“§ 209.009. (a) A property owners’ association may foreclose a lien on a property owner’s lot under the association’s declaration or other governing documents only if the association has provided the property owner with notice of the delinquency and an opportunity to cure.”

The Association has complied with all notice requirements. You were sent a demand letter on January 10, 2025, and a second notice on February 20, 2025. To date, no payment has been received.

The Association is represented by its legal counsel, Mr. James R. Holloway of Holloway, Lynch & Park, LLP, 2000 Louisiana Street, Suite 400, Houston, Texas 77002, telephone (713) 555-0298, email j.holloway@hlplegal.com. Any communications regarding this matter should be directed to Mr. Holloway.

If the full balance is not paid within thirty (30) days from the date of this letter, the Association will initiate foreclosure proceedings. A hearing will be held before the Association’s Board of Directors on May 5, 2025, at 6:30 p.m. at the Sunflower Ridge Clubhouse, 100 Sunflower Lane, Houston, Texas. You have the right to attend and to be represented by counsel.

The Association may also seek a judicial foreclosure in the 113th Judicial District Court of Harris County, Texas, styled Sunflower Ridge Homeowners Association, Inc. v. William Ferguson and Patricia Ferguson, Docket No. 2025-12345. The Association’s right to foreclose was affirmed in In re Sunflower Ridge Assessment Lien, 567 S.W.3d 456 (Tex. App.—Houston [1st Dist.] 2023). See also Meadowbrook HOA v. Torres, 890 S.W.3d 234 (Tex. App.—Houston [14th Dist.] 2021).

Your Social Security numbers on record: William: 789-01-2345; Patricia: 789 01 2346. Your date of birth as shown on your membership application: William: June 14, 1968; Patricia: November 30, 1970.

Please remit payment via certified funds to the Association’s management office, Attention: Ms. Cynthia R. Bell, Property Manager, at the address above, or contact her at (713) 555-0356 or c.bell@sunflowerridgehoa.org.

This notice affects the property of A.B., a minor, who resides at 892 Oak Hollow Drive, but A.B. is not a named party in this enforcement.

Sincerely,

Sunflower Ridge Homeowners Association, Inc.
By: Thomas J. Mitchell, Secretary

Enclosures: Account Statement, Copy of Declaration, Demand Letters

title: Hearing Notice – Architectural Modification Denial and Fine Imposition
text:
OAK MEADOWS COMMUNITY ASSOCIATION, INC.

NOTICE OF HEARING AND PROPOSED FINE

Cause No. 2025-CV-00389

To: Dr. Samantha K. Reeves and Mr. Michael D. Reeves
456 Elm Street, Unit 7
Dallas, Texas 75201

From: Oak Meadows Community Association, Inc.
Date: April 20, 2025

RE: Unapproved Shed Structure – Lot 8, Phase II

Dear Dr. Reeves and Mr. Reeves:

This is to notify you that the Oak Meadows Community Association (the “Association”) has denied your application for an architectural modification to construct a storage shed on Lot 8. The denial was based on the finding that the proposed shed would exceed the height limitation set forth in Section 4.5(b) of the Association’s Architectural Guidelines.

Despite the denial, you have constructed a shed measuring approximately 10 feet in height, which is two feet above the allowed maximum. This constitutes a violation of the governing documents. Pursuant to Section 5.2 of the Bylaws and Texas Property Code § 204.010(a), the Association is authorized to impose fines for such violations. The applicable statute provides:

“§ 204.010. (a) A property owners’ association may impose a fine on a property owner for a violation of the association’s governing documents if the association provides the owner with notice and an opportunity to be heard.”

The Association has scheduled a hearing before the Board of Directors on May 12, 2025, at 7:30 p.m. at the Oak Meadows Community Center, 555 Oak Park Drive, Dallas, Texas. You may appear in person or through counsel to present evidence. The proposed fine is $250 per day, retroactive to March 1, 2025, for a total of $12,500 as of this date.

The Association is represented by Ms. Angela M. Torres of Torres & Nguyen, LLC, 300 Main Street, Suite 1200, Dallas, Texas 75202, telephone (214) 555-0411, email a.torres@torresnguyen.com. Please direct all communications to Ms. Torres.

If you fail to attend the hearing or fail to remove the shed within fifteen (15) days thereafter, the Association will file a lawsuit in the 191st Judicial District Court of Dallas County, Texas, styled Oak Meadows Community Association, Inc. v. Samantha Reeves and Michael Reeves, Docket No. DC-25-04567. The Association will seek an injunction, fines, and attorney’s fees. A similar case, Cypress Village HOA v. Nguyen, 678 S.W.3d 901 (Tex. App.—Dallas 2024), supports the enforcement of architectural restrictions. See also In re Oak Meadows Fine Dispute, 345 S.W.3d 678 (Tex. App.—Dallas 2022).

Your Social Security numbers on file: Samantha: 321-54-9876; Michael: 321 54 9877. Date of birth: Samantha: December 5, 1980; Michael: January 12, 1978.

For questions, please contact the Association’s compliance officer, Mr. David L. Franklin, at (214) 555-0622 or d.franklin@oakmeadowsassoc.org.

This notice also pertains to the property of A.B., a minor who resides at 458 Elm Street, but A.B. is not a party to this action.

Sincerely,

Oak Meadows Community Association, Inc.
By: Patricia H. Nguyen, Vice President

Enclosures: Denial Letter, Architectural Guidelines Excerpt, Photographs

title: Demand for Compliance – Prohibited Vehicle Parking
text:
CEDAR PARK CONDOMINIUM OWNERS ASSOCIATION, INC.

DEMAND FOR COMPLIANCE AND NOTICE OF FINE

Cause No. 2025-CV-00572

To: Mr. Steven J. Kowalski and Ms. Emily R. Kowalski
78 Cypress Court, Unit 4
San Antonio, Texas 78201

From: Cedar Park Condominium Owners Association, Inc.
Date: May 5, 2025

RE: Violation of Parking Rules – Prohibited Vehicle Storage

Dear Mr. Kowalski and Ms. Kowalski:

This is to demand that you immediately cease the storage of a recreational vehicle (RV) in the visitor parking area of the Cedar Park Condominium complex, as such storage violates Section 7.1 of the Condominium’s Rules and Regulations. The relevant provision states:

“§ 7.1. No owner or resident shall park or store any recreational vehicle, boat, trailer, or commercial vehicle in any parking space designated for visitor use. Such vehicles shall be stored only in designated storage areas or within an enclosed garage.”

The RV, a 2023 Forest River model, has been observed on multiple occasions in space #14 since March 15, 2025. You were previously issued a warning on March 20, 2025, but the violation persists.

The Association is represented by counsel, Ms. Lisa M. Greenfield of Greenfield & Associates, P.C., 700 Riverwalk Boulevard, Suite 300, San Antonio, Texas 78205, telephone (210) 555-0177, email l.greenfield@greenfieldlegal.com. All correspondence should be directed to Ms. Greenfield.

A hearing before the Board of Directors is scheduled for May 20, 2025, at 6:00 p.m. at the Cedar Park Clubhouse, 77 Cypress Court, San Antonio, Texas. You may appear and present evidence. The Association proposes a fine of $100 per day for each day the RV remains in violation, commencing April 1, 2025, for a total of $3,500 as of this date.

If you fail to comply, the Association will seek enforcement in the 45th Judicial District Court of Bexar County, Texas, styled Cedar Park Condominium Owners Association, Inc. v. Steven Kowalski and Emily Kowalski, Docket No. 2025-CI-07890. The Association may seek injunctive relief, monetary damages, and attorney’s fees. The authority of an HOA to enforce parking restrictions was upheld in Stonebridge HOA v. Patel, 234 S.W.3d 567 (Tex. App.—San Antonio 2020). See also In re Cedar Park Parking Violation, 901 S.W.3d 345 (Tex. App.—San Antonio 2023).

Your Social Security numbers on file: Steven: 987-65-4321; Emily: 987 65 4322. Your dates of birth: Steven: October 10, 1972; Emily: February 14, 1975.

For questions, please contact the Association’s property manager, Mr. Mark T. Wilson, at (210) 555-0889 or m.wilson@cedarparkcondos.org.

This notice also concerns the unit of A.B., a minor who lives at 80 Cypress Court, Unit 5, but A.B. is not a party.

Sincerely,

Cedar Park Condominium Owners Association, Inc.
By: Karen L. Johnson, Treasurer

Enclosures: Rule Excerpt, Photographs of RV, Warning Letter

title: Notice of Special Assessment and Lien Threat
text:
BLUEBERRY HILL HOMEOWNERS ASSOCIATION, INC.

NOTICE OF SPECIAL ASSESSMENT AND POTENTIAL LIEN

Cause No. 2025-CV-00614

To: Mr. Gregory A. Whitfield and Ms. Donna L. Whitfield
12 Blueberry Lane
Fort Worth, Texas 76102

From: Blueberry Hill Homeowners Association, Inc.
Date: May 18, 2025

RE: Special Assessment for Common Area Repairs – Lot 22

Dear Mr. Whitfield and Ms. Whitfield:

This letter serves as official notice that the Board of Directors of the Blueberry Hill Homeowners Association (the “Association”) has approved a special assessment in the amount of $2,500 per lot, payable in full by June 30, 2025, for the purpose of repairing the community swimming pool and clubhouse roof. The assessment was approved at a duly called board meeting on April 25, 2025, pursuant to Article VI, Section 6.3 of the Association’s Bylaws and Texas Property Code § 204.005, which provides:

“§ 204.005. (a) A property owners’ association may impose a special assessment on all property owners in a subdivision or development for the purpose of defraying, in whole or in part, the cost of any construction, repair, or replacement of a capital improvement.”

Your account reflects that as of the date of this letter, the special assessment remains unpaid, along with prior delinquent regular assessments totaling $1,200. The total due is $3,700. If payment is not received by June 30, 2025, the Association will record a lien against Lot 22 and may proceed with foreclosure.

The Association is represented by its legal counsel, Mr. Brian K. Walsh of Walsh & Martinez, LLP, 500 Commerce Street, Suite 1500, Fort Worth, Texas 76102, telephone (817) 555-0234, email b.walsh@walshmartinez.com. Please direct all communications to Mr. Walsh.

You have the right to request a hearing before the Board of Directors to contest the assessment. A hearing is scheduled for June 10, 2025, at 7:00 p.m. at the Blueberry Hill Community Center, 1 Blueberry Hill Drive, Fort Worth, Texas. If you fail to appear, the assessment will be deemed final.

If necessary, the Association will file a lawsuit in the 348th Judicial District Court of Tarrant County, Texas, styled Blueberry Hill Homeowners Association, Inc. v. Gregory Whitfield and Donna Whitfield, Docket No. 2025-34567. The Association may seek a judgment for the amounts due, foreclosure, and attorney’s fees. The enforceability of special assessments was confirmed in Lakewood HOA v. Jackson, 567 S.W.3d 890 (Tex. App.—Fort Worth 2021). See also In re Blueberry Hill Special Assessment, 456 S.W.3d 123 (Tex. App.—Fort Worth 2023).

Your Social Security numbers on record: Gregory: 123-45-6789; Donna: 123 45 6790. Date of birth: Gregory: August 3, 1965; Donna: April 19, 1967.

For inquiries, contact the Association’s manager, Ms. Nancy J. Carter, at (817) 555-0345 or n.carter@blueberryhillhoa.org.

This notice may affect the property of A.B., a minor residing at 14 Blueberry Lane, but A.B. is not a party to this assessment.

Sincerely,

Blueberry Hill Homeowners Association, Inc.
By: Charles R. Henderson, President

Enclosures: Board Resolution, Payment Coupon, Bylaws Excerpt
